This position is located at the Clement J. Zablocki VA Medical Center, Milwaukee, Wisconsin in the Geriatrics and Extended Care (GEC) Division.

Incumbent will be assigned to work in the Division's main office.The incumbent will receive direction from the Supervisory Program Specialist and is responsible for providing administrative support in the Office of the Division Manager.

The incumbent will interface with personal computer (PC) applications to include, but not limited to: VA Time and Attendance System (VATAS), Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VISTA), HR Smart, Electronic Personnel Access System (ePAS), Microsoft Office programs.This position is the target in the line of progression of PSAs assigned to GEC.

Major Duties: Conducts quarterly documentation audits and tracks trends in program compliance; Generates and analyzes key performance reports to identify operational gaps or strengths; Maintains a database of corrective actions and monitors closure timelines; provides basic policy interpretations and prepares procedural updates for staff; coordinates and documents monthly compliance and performance review meetings.

Builds and maintains operational dashboards for programs and administrative functions; Performs monthly and quarterly data reviews to support planning and improvement; Creates summary visuals (charts, graphs, tables) to communicate findings; Onboards new administrative team members using standardized training tools; conducts quarterly workshops on updated policies, tools, and best practices; Serves as a peer mentor for GS-5 and GS-4 staff; facilitates knowledge sharing; tracks training completions and provides status updates to supervisors; Supports creation and revision of SOPs for common administrative processes.

Maintains calendars for major initiatives; coordinates timelines and stakeholder tasks; prepares meeting agendas, collects documentation, and follows up on action items; Drafts memos, procedural updates, and internal bulletins for distribution; Responds to routine inquiries related to scheduling, compliance, or procedures; Provides occasional MSA coverage in inpatient areas to support patient movement, document handling, or front desk inquiries.

Manages timecards for complex 24/7 inpatient schedules across T38, HT38, and TS employees; validates leave, overtime, and tour changes in VATAS; Resolves discrepancies; provides biweekly and monthly reports on attendance, OT usage, and variances Holds and manages a Government Purchase Card (GPC) to execute authorized micro-purchases for the unit or Division; Submits supply and service orders that align with approved needs and complies with VA procurement policies; Reconciles monthly purchase card statements in a timely and accurate manner; Resolves discrepancies with vendors or fiscal staff; tracks and reports purchase trends to identify recurring needs or cost-saving opportunities; Serves as a backup purchasing resource for other GEC units when requested by the supervisor Promotion Potential: The selectee may be promoted to the full performance level without further competition when all regulatory, qualification, and performance requirements are met.

Selection at a lower grade level does not guarantee promotion to the full performance level. Work Schedule: Monday- Friday, 7:30am- 4:00pm Telework: Ad-hoc, available Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Position Description/PD#: Program Support Assistant/PD25337A and PD253364 Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized.

Critical Skills Incentive (CSI): Not Authorized. Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized. PCS Appraised Value Offer (AVO): Not Authorized.
To qualify for this position, applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement, 08/06/2026. Time-In-Grade Requirement: Applicants who are current Federal employees and have held a GS grade any time in the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

For a GS-6 position you must have served 52 weeks at the GS-5 level. The grade may have been in any occupation, but must have been held in the Federal service. An SF-50 that shows your time-in-grade eligibility must be submitted with your application materials.

If the most recent SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you possess one-year time-in-grade, as required by the announcement. In this instance, you must provide an additional SF-50 that clearly demonstrates one-year time-in-grade.

Note: Time-In-Grade requirements also apply to former Federal employees applying for reinstatement as well as current employees applying for Veterans Employment Opportunities Act of 1998 (VEOA) appointment.

You may qualify based on your experience and/or education as described below: GS-5 Specialized Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade GS-4 in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization.

Examples of specialized experience would typically include, but are not limited to: Strong communication and interpersonal skills to coordinate with staff across clinical and administrative areas. Detailed knowledge of privacy, confidentiality, and data protection laws including HIPAA, the Privacy Act, and VA information security policies.

Familiarity with VA performance improvement principles, safety practices, infection control standards, and equipment use in a healthcare setting.

Coordinate meeting logistics, prepare agendas, manage correspondence, and maintain time-sensitive documents with minimal supervision. -OR- Education: Applicants may substitute education for the required experience.

To qualify based on education for this grade level you must have successfully completed full 4-year course of study, above high school, leading to a bachelor's degree in a field for which high school graduation or the equivalent is the normal pre-requisite. NOTE: Transcripts must be submitted with application.

Education cannot be credited without documentation -OR- Combination: Applicants may also combine education and experience to qualify at this level.

You must have equivalent combination of successfully completed post-high school education and specialized experience directly related to the work of the position as outlined above that meets the requirements of the position. NOTE: If using education combined with specialized experience to qualify, a copy of your transcript is required.

GS-6 Specialized Experience: You must have at least one (1) full year of specialized experience at the GS-5 level that equipped you with the knowledge, skills and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the Program Support Assistant position, and that is typically in or related to the duties of this position.

Specialized experience includes: Strong communication and interpersonal skills to coordinate with staff across clinical and administrative areas. Detailed knowledge of privacy, confidentiality, and data protection laws including HIPAA, the Privacy Act, and VA information security policies.

Familiarity with VA performance improvement principles, safety practices, infection control standards, and equipment use in a healthcare setting. Coordinate meeting logistics, prepare agendas, manage correspondence, and maintain time-sensitive documents with minimal supervision.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook), SharePoint, and VA systems such as VistA, VATAS, BMS, and HR Smart, with the ability to extract and compile operational data.

Working with scheduling systems, time and leave policies for Title 5 and Title 38 employees, and the ability to reconcile complex schedules with varied tours, pay entitlements, and leave statuses. Data entry, document formatting, proofreading, and written communication using VA standards and terminology.

For more information on these qualification standards, please visit the United States Office of Personnel Management's website at https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/.

We are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Administrative Specialist to provide comprehensive administrative and operational support across multiple departments. The ideal candidate will coordinate schedules, manage documentation, maintain accurate records, prepare reports, and help ensure efficient day-to-day business operations.
Key Responsibilities Provide administrative support to managers, executives, and department teams.
Coordinate calendars, appointments, meetings, and virtual conferences.
Prepare reports, presentations, spreadsheets, and professional correspondence.
Maintain accurate electronic records, databases, and confidential documents.
Perform data entry and verify the accuracy of business information.
Respond to emails, phone calls, and internal inquiries professionally.
Coordinate travel arrangements, meeting logistics, and administrative projects.
Assist with onboarding documentation and employee administrative processes.
Support cross-functional projects and process improvement initiatives.
Maintain compliance with company policies and administrative procedures.
Perform other administrative duties and special projects as assigned.
Required Qualifications Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Business Administration or a related field preferred.
Minimum 2 years of experience in administrative support, office administration, or a similar role.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
Familiarity with Google Workspace and online collaboration tools.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational, multitasking, and time management abilities.
High attention to detail and ability to maintain confidentiality.
Ability to work independently in a remote work environment.

The primary purpose of this position is to provide clerical support and perform routine administrative tasks to assist HR Assistants and HR Specialists assigned to the NAF personnel office. Recruitment & Placement: Utilizes automated recruitment tool. Builds and edits user accounts. Generates vacancies for job announcements.

Enters applicable position and organizational data for vacancy. Creates job opportunity announcements. Verifies applicant eligibilities in accordance with applicable laws, policies, and procedures. Produces applicant lists for selecting official. Performs onboarding tasks. Initiates and monitors local installation records checks.

May initiate background investigations in NBIS and build employee profile in CSO IT. Monitors status of background investigations. Conducts in-processing briefing. Assists in the completion of employment documents. Position Management: Enters classified position descriptions into automated library.

Verifies signatures on position descriptions and the most up-to-date Standardized Position Descriptions and Position Guides are being used. Uploads supporting documents (i.e., evaluation statement; org chart; position designation tool (PDT) result, etc.) into the position description casefile/record. Locates position descriptions in the library.

Routes all classification requests to appropriate point of contact. DCPDS: Enters personnel data into an automated personnel data system. Completes applicant and position builds using data provided. Verifies documentation for personnel action. Codes personnel actions in accordance with applicable policies and procedures.

Processes a variety of personnel requests and actions. Generates personnel reports. Identifies and corrects discrepancies in personnel data. Clerical/Admin: Performs front desk responsibilities. Provides customer service assistance to customers. Makes copies, scans documents, uploads and files documents. Distributes copies of personnel actions.

Provides general information regarding position vacancies, application procedures, etc. Operates a computer remote terminal and word processing equipment. Receives and checks documents for completion and accuracy in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. Contacts appropriate sources to secure missing data or documents.

Prepares in-processing documents. Creates and maintains position control registers, office files, group insurance files, etc. May requisition forms and post changes to directives. Assists applicants with system errors when applying for vacancies. Elevates complex system issues to senior HR staff. Prepares and submits payroll transmittals.

Performs other related duties as assigned. If interested in applying for this position you may preview the online application: https://apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/13001844

Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if the position allows for qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application.

Qualifying Experience: Experience performing clerical work and providing customer service to internal and external customers; applying rules, regulations, and procedures in accomplishment of clerical/administrative work; utilizing office automation software (MS Windows, MS Office, including PowerPoint, Word, Access, and Excel).

Condition(s) of Employment: Successful completion and favorable adjudication of a Tier 3 background investigation is required. Successful completion of Training Checklist and mastery of skills within 6 months of employment is required. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas:

You will serve as the subject matter expert on policies and procedures related to officer applications, orders, data input, and the processing, retention, and commissioning of officer applicants.
You will coordinate and administer the Officer Procurement Programs within the Marine Corps District Area of Operation.
You will be responsible for the training and development of recruiting personnel, ensuring adherence to administrative procedures, program functionality, and quality control of officer applications.
You will ensure officer candidate data, databases, files, and historical statistics are maintained; prepare orders for summer training; and process Officer Candidate School drop reports.
You will prepare correspondence, lists, vouchers, reports, email correspondence, and memoranda in accordance with established Navy and Marine Corps manuals and ensure timely processing of incoming and outgoing mail.
You will provide analytical data and analysis to evaluate program performance and quality control measures.
Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-07 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Performing administrative and clerical support duties, including processing applicant packages, administering background screenings, reviewing documents for accuracy and completeness, managing administrative workflows, drafting written correspondence, communicating with internal and external stakeholders, and using office automation tools.

Manage the daily administrative operations of the Executive Office, serving as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and handling highly sensitive and confidential information.
Serve as a critical backup for civilian payroll and personnel systems globally, processing time and attendance, performance appraisals, and complex pay-related actions.
Control the flow of information by screening incoming mail, independently drafting responses to general inquiries, and reviewing all outgoing correspondence for accuracy and formatting.
Research and compile data from various sources to create technical reports, statistical charts, and executive briefing materials using software like Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Coordinate logistics for high-level meetings and conferences, including preparing background materials, tracking agendas, recording minutes, and managing protocols for senior-level visitors.
Arrange comprehensive travel requirements for executive staff, coordinate trip logistics, and process travel vouchers and reports upon completion of travel.

For GS-07: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Assisting in the coordination of day-to-day administrative operations for an office; 2) Preparing, formatting, and routing correspondence, reports, and meeting materials; 3) Processing standard administrative actions (such as travel orders, time and attendance, or routine personnel requests) using automated systems; and 4) Gathering and assembling data from various databases to support office operations.

This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service, GS-06. OR Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as business management/administration.

OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12.

Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages.

For GS-08: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Independently managing comprehensive administrative and operational activities for an executive or senior-level office; 2) Advising management and staff on administrative policies, procedures, and systems (e.g., travel, personnel, or payroll operations); 3) Reviewing, consolidating, and composing complex or sensitive reports, briefing materials, and correspondence for senior leadership; and 4) Serving as a primary technical point of contact to troubleshoot and resolve issues within automated administrative systems (e.g., financial, payroll, or personnel databases).

This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service, GS-07. OR Education: One and a half years of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position.

OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12.

Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond one year (total semester hours minus 18) by 9. Add the two percentages.

GS-07: Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-06).

GS-08: Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-07).

As a Supervisory Administrative Officer, you will perform the following duties: Serve as a senior advisor to office Deputy and Director, leading programmatic support of effective management of fishery resources. Provide expert advice and guidance for the formulation of program operation, administrative, and regulatory policies.

Oversee the allocation and distribution of finances and budgets for the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS). Responsible for all technical and administrative responsibilities and functions such as procurement, acquisition, records management, property, and human resources.

Participate and collaborate in long and short-range management analysis, action plans and execution. Ensure office goals and objectives are aligned with the agency's objectives. Coordinate assigned resources to execute assigned programs and projects within associated physical and fiscal constraints.

Exercise full supervisory authority over a diverse group of employees, include planning and distributing work, setting priorities, and developing schedules for the completion of work. Evaluate the performance of subordinates and provide technical oversight and instruction. Identify developmental need and provide or arrange for training.

This position will be filled under the DOC Alternative Personnel System (CAPS). Under CAPS, positions are classified by career, pay plan, and pay band. The ZA-5 is equivalent to the GS-15.
Qualification requirements in the vacancy announcements are based on the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards Handbook, which contains federal qualification standards.

This handbook is available on the Office of Personnel Management's website located at: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/ EDUCATION: There is no positive education requirement for this position.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent in difficulty and responsibility to the next lower grade level in the Federal Service.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped the applicant with the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position. This experience need not have been in the federal government.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations e.g., professional; philanthropic, religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies; knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

To qualify at the ZA-5 or GS-15 level: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must possess one full year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the ZA-4 or GS-14 in the Federal service.

Specialized experience MUST include all of the following: Establishing objectives and assessing progress of operational program areas to ensure effective use of resources in support of fisheries management; Planning and implementing organizational wide policies, procedures, programs, initiatives supporting human capital and administrative operations support; and Overseeing or managing administrative support programs, such as procurement, acquisition, records management, property management, or human resources; and Developing annual, multiyear, or other long-range strategic or tactical plans.

Depuis plus de 40 ans, notre entreprise familiale de paysagisme est reconnue à Genève pour la qualité de ses prestations, son professionnalisme et la relation de confiance qu'elle entretient avec sa clientè d'accompagner notre développement, nous recherchons une Assistante administrative et technique expérimentée, capable d'évoluer dans un environnement exigeant où la qualité, la rigueur et le sens du service sont des valeurs essentielles.
Votre mission
En collaboration directe avec la Direction, vous occuperez un rôle central dans le bon fonctionnement administratif de l' principales responsabilités seront notamment les suivantes :Assurer l'accueil téléphonique et le suivi de la clientèle avec professionnalisme et édiger des courriers, devis, offres et correspondances de qualité.Assurer le suivi administratif des chantiers.Gestion du parc véhicule.Assurer le suivi administratif des employés (fiches horaires, vacances, entrée et sortie du personnels).Préparer la facturation et assurer le suivi des érer les dossiers clients, les commandes et les documents administratifs.Collaborer étroitement avec les techniciens et la Direction.Organiser les priorités et gérer simultanément plusieurs dossiers.Entretenir des contacts réguliers avec les clients, régies, architectes, fournisseurs et partenaires.Participer activement à l'amélioration continue de l'organisation administrative.
Votre profil
Vous êtes une personne fiable, organisée, proactive et autonome, qui apprécie le travail bien fait et possède un excellent sens du service.
Vous disposez notamment des compétences suivantes : CFC d'employé(e) de commerce ou formation jugée équivalente.
Minimum 5 années d'expérience dans une fonction similaire (secteur du bâtiment, du paysagisme, de la construction ou de l'immobilier : un réel atout).
Excellente maîtrise du français, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit, avec une orthographe irréprochable.
Excellentes capacités rédactionnelles et aisance dans la rédaction de courriers professionnels.
Bonne maîtrise de l'anglais, à l'oral comme à l'écrit.Excellente maîtrise de Microsoft Word, Excel et du logiciel Winbiz.
Très bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques usuels.
Capacité à gérer les priorités, à anticiper et à travailler avec un haut niveau d'autonomie.
Sens aigu de l'organisation, de la confidentialité et des responsabilités.Excellente présentation, aisance relationnelle et sens du service.
Aisance dans les échanges avec une clientèle exigeante, des régies immobilières, des architectes et différents partenaires.
Esprit d'équipe, flexibilité et volonté de s'investir durablement dans une entreprise.
Saisie comptables des factures créancièresAdministration RH liée en coordination avec le prestataire de paie.
Ce que nous vous offrons
Un poste stable au sein d'une entreprise familiale reconnue à Genève depuis plus de 40 ans.
Une collaboration directe avec la Direction et une réelle autonomie dans vos responsabilités.
Un environnement de travail agréable, dynamique et à taille activité variée, valorisante et stimulante.
Une entreprise où la qualité du travail, le respect des collaborateurs et la satisfaction des clients sont des priorités.
Si vous aimez les responsabilités, que vous êtes rigoureuse, proactive, que vous avez le sens du détail et souhaitez vous investir durablement dans une entreprise où votre travail fera réellement la différence, nous nous réjouissons de recevoir votre dossier complet de candidature (CV, lettre de motivation, certificats de travail et diplômes).

You will lead post-award conferences, negotiate contract modifications, and manage procurement system accounts (Navy-ERP, WAWF, PD2).
You will coordinate Contracting Officer Representative (COR) functions across commands and independently resolve complex contracting disputes.
You will provide regulatory procurement advice to command leadership in coordination with legal counsel.
You will manage procurement strategies, policies, and tuition compliance for NROTC Educational Service Agreements (ESAs) with universities.
You will formulate long-range educational procurement plans and evaluate state and federal legal applicability.
You will train and evaluate domain CORs and Technical Assistants on contract compliance and oversight procedures.
You will investigate labor and performance issues, review claims, determine allowable costs, dispose of government property, and finalize contract closeouts.
You will lead hiring efforts, identify training opportunities, and resolve employee grievances under EEO guidelines.
In addition to the Basic Requirements for this position, your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Applying contract administration principles to manage and oversee complex contract types, such as fixed-price, cost-reimbursement, and incentive contracts, throughout the entire acquisition lifecycle; 2) Conducting price and cost analysis on proposals to establish negotiation positions, resolve invoice issues, and process modifications; 3) Managing contract terminations (convenience or default) by evaluating settlement proposals, resolving disputes, and executing closeouts; 4) Developing and implementing quality assurance surveillance plans (QASPs) and utilizing various oversight techniques to monitor and evaluate contractor performance against technical and administrative contract requirements; 5) Interpreting and applying federal and state laws impacting tuition policies and agreements to administer contracts and Educational Service Agreements (ESAs) with colleges and universities.

NOTE: All experience must be fully demonstrated in your resume to be considered for the position. This is a Defense Acquisition Workforce position that requires a Contracting, Foundational acquisition certification. The incumbent has 36 months to earn this certification.

Incumbent must obtain and maintain certification in accordance with DoD Instruction 5000.66. Acquisition Workforce (AWF) members must complete 80 hours of Continuous Learning Points (CLPs) every two (2) years, in accordance with DoDI 5000.66.

Workforce members are encouraged to earn their CLPs by completing Defense Acquisition University (DAU) Credentials. Obtaining certification within the allotted grace period and maintaining CLPs before and after achieving certification are conditions of employment.

Failure to meet these requirements could result in disciplinary action and/or removal from employment.

Maintains a detailed knowledge of travel policies and regulations to serve as a technical resource to unit personnel.
Prepares travel requests and vouchers for travel.
Advises on travel allowances and requirement and ensures adherence to travel regulations.
Uses automated systems and software for travel and voucher preparation.
Provides support for grants and agreements on the Ranger District.
Develops and implements new systems or administrative processes to meet unit needs.
In order to qualify, you must meet the eligibility and qualifications requirements as defined below by the closing date of the announcement. For more information on the qualifications for this position, visit the Office of Personnel Management's General Schedule Qualification Standards.

Specialized Experience Requirement: For the GS-06 grade level: You must have one year specialized experience equivalent to the GS-05 grade level in the Federal service.

Specialized experience is defined as one or more of the following: Provided support and assistance processing a wide variety of requisitions; reconciled purchases and maintained files; Processed incoming and outgoing mail; Established and maintained the office files, accountable property inventories, records, etc.

(hardcopy and/or electronic format); and/or used automated software to produces reports, correspondence and other written documents in draft form. For the GS-07 grade level: You must have one year specialized experience equivalent to the GS-06 grade level in the Federal Service.

Specialized experience is defined as two or more of the following: Carried out new systems or administrative processes to meet business needs; received and reviewed all formal ingoing/outgoing correspondence for proper format, grammar, punctuation, etc.; used automated databases and software to produce reports and record information; established and maintained manual and electronic records and filing systems; and/or produced written documentation, reports, memos, etc. in final format.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Als eines der führenden Technologieunternehmen beschäftigt Siemens in der Schweiz rund 6000 Mitarbeitende. Mit unseren wegweisenden Lösungen in den Bereichen Gebäudetechnik, Energie, Mobilität, Gesundheit und Industrie gestalten wir die Zukunft.
In unserem \#TeamSiemens bist du das Organisationstalent deiner Abteilung. Dank unseres Netzwerks FutureAssistants@Siemens kannst du dich mit anderen Assistent:innen austauschen, dich weiterbilden und weltweit vernetzen. Bewirb dich noch heute als **Team Assistant** - dein Team freut sich auf dich!
**Deine neuen Aufgaben**
* Du übernimmst die vollständige Abwicklung von Material- und Dienstleistungsbestellungen, bist dabei zentrale Ansprechperson und gewährleistest einen reibungslosen Ablauf von der Bestellung bis zur Rechnungsbearbeitung

* Im Rahmen deiner organisatorischen Verantwortung planst und koordinierst du Meetings, Events, Schulungen sowie Workshops und sorgst für die termingerechte Reservation aller Ressourcen
* Darauf aufbauend organisierst du Geschäftsreisen für Mitarbeitende, inklusive Visumsbeschaffung und Einladungsschreiben, und kontrollierst die wöchentlichen Zeitrapporte im SAP-System
* Abschliessend unterstützt du bei Ein- und Austritten von Mitarbeitenden durch die strukturierte Abwicklung aller administrativen Prozesse und koordinierst Interviewtermine zur Sicherstellung eines professionellen Recruiting-Prozesses
**Deine Talente und Erfahrungen**
* Du hast eine abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation und bringst idealerweise erste Berufserfahrung im Bereich Logistik oder Administration mit
* Du verfügst über fundierte Kenntnisse im Umgang mit MS Office und SAP und bist sicher in der Abwicklung administrativer Prozesse
* Du zeichnest dich durch einen freundlichen, souveränen und serviceorientierten Umgang mit Kolleg:innen sowie externen Partner:innen aus
* Du bist bereit, an vier Tagen pro Woche im Office zu arbeiten
* Deine Arbeitsweise ist zuverlässig, termingerecht, sorgfältig und auch in hektischen Situationen behältst du den Überblick
* Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift runden dein Profil ab
**Deine Vorteile**
* Mobilitätspauschale
* Vielfältige Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten
* Zugang zu Aktienplänen für Mitarbeitende
* Alle Vorteile findest du hier
**Unsere Unternehmenskultur - dein neues Arbeitsumfeld**
Die Kultur bei Siemens Schweiz ist mehr als nur ein Arbeitsumfeld - sie ist das Herzstück unseres täglichen Miteinanders und der Schlüssel zu unserem Erfolg. Siemens Schweiz bietet ein zukunftsorientiertes Arbeitsumfeld, das von Innovation, Nachhaltigkeit und persönlicher Entfaltung geprägt ist.

Wir zeichnen uns durch Eigenverantwortung, Chancengerechtigkeit und Vielfalt aus, in der sich jede:r Mitarbeitende authentisch einbringen kann. Flexible Arbeitsmodelle und mobiles Arbeiten sind bei uns gelebte Realität und ermöglichen unseren Mitarbeitenden eine ausgewogene Work-Life-Balance.
